annotation.summary_en: A handyman discusses paint colors for a living room and bedroom with a couple, insensitive to the fact that the husband's father is dying.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch takes place in a bare, unfinished apartment under renovation. A handyman wearing a traditional paper painter's hat is discussing interior design choices with a man in a white shirt and a woman. In the first scene, they discuss the living room ('zal'). The handyman suggests a bright, neutral 'orange' (aranzhvi) to please all types of guests, from doctors to police officers. However, the husband becomes furious, revealing that his father is in critical condition and they expect a wake soon. The handyman insensitively pivots, suggesting they paint the walls a 'dark brown' (karichvi) to match the mourning period, the funeral, and the memorial services (7 days, 40 days, one year). He suggests that after the mourning cycle and the holiday of Vardavar are over, he will return to repaint it orange so the household can be happy again. In the second scene, they move to the bedroom ('spalni'). They discuss white oak furniture and lemon-colored walls. When deciding on the ceiling color, the handyman makes a crude joke implying that the wife's opinion matters most for the ceiling because she spends the most time looking up at it while in bed.
